title: Al-Jami', the Gatherer
hookLine: the Gatherer, who will gather all
tomorrow: if God needs nothing, why does Dadi pray at all?

lines: NEVER IN ONE PLACE, NOW IN ONE PLACE.
cards: Saturday morning. Drop cloths, a borrowed ladder, a stack of paint cans by a tagged wall. Yesterday's question was who shows up.

For Amira, the answer: her dad, Jordan, a thirteen-year-old in an old t-shirt, two neighbors nobody invited, and Dadi with a pot of food. People who'd never have stood in one place, standing in one place.
That's today's Name in miniature. Al-Jami', the Gatherer.

teach.b: Al-Jami', the Gatherer, who will gather all. The Qur'an speaks of a Day when Allah gathers all people together.

teach.h: NATIONS AND TRIBES, TO KNOW ONE ANOTHER.
teach.b: And it speaks about gathering in this life, too, in a verse addressed to everyone: "O mankind! Lo! We have created you male and female, and have made you nations and tribes that ye may know one another."
Here's the line to tell a friend tonight: the verse doesn't say we were made different so we'd keep apart. It says so we'd come to know one another.
Now the week, gathered on one wall. The Requiter: no wrong forgotten, so Amira never had to carry the payback herself. The Pardoner: erased, the way her dad wiped the grudge on the first morning.
The Most Kind: tender, which turned out not to mean silent. Owner of all: a wall that was only ever on loan.
Lord of Majesty and Generosity: a hot chocolate at the counter. The Equitable: a share a thirteen-year-old can carry, which today looks like a roller and a long wall.
Six Names, and they all ended up standing on the same drop cloth.

how: Muslims gather each week for the Friday prayer, jumu'ah, and gather families and neighbors around shared meals at Eid.

o: the Keeper, who stores every deed
the Divider, who sorts good from bad
the Gatherer, who brings all together

games.q: the week's Names on one wall — tap the pairs.

s: the Qur'an says people were made nations and tribes so they'd know one another
"O mankind! Lo! We have created you male and female, and have made you nations and tribes that ye may know one another."
pardoning someone means acting as if the wrong never happened
Al-'Afuww wipes the trace of the grudge; the wall still got repainted.
tender means never saying anything hard
Ar-Ra'uf feels another's weight; the one described as full of pity still spoke hard truths.

games.q: a new kid sits down at your lunch table and your friends go quiet. what does today's verse point you toward?
o: made different to know one another: ask them a real question.
people are happiest with their own group; let them find theirs.
act like there are no differences between any of you at all.
games.why: 49:13 doesn't erase the differences or wall them off. it gives them a purpose: that ye may know one another.

practice: Count on your fingers the people who would come if you asked for help on a Saturday, one finger for each, and for every one of them a silent thank you. Then let one face stay with you: someone you haven't gathered with in a while.
Hold them in mind until the bell.

wordCard.voice: Al-Jami'. The Gatherer, who brings together what's scattered, and who will gather all.

orig.note: Arabic: the Gatherer, a Name of Allah; 3:9 calls Him the one who gathers mankind.

carryVoice: Keep this one: he gathers, the ones you'd invite and the ones you never would. A week of Names, gathered.

sources.q: O mankind! Lo! We have created you male and female, and have made you nations and tribes that ye may know one another.

sources.ref: Qur'an 3:9 (Allah gathers mankind to a Day)
